Causeway
kawz´wā
n. (a raised road or ascent to the temple gate — Hebrew mesillah, a highway)
From Old French chaucie, a raised road, ultimately from Latin calx, limestone. The Hebrew mesillah is a built-up highway — a road raised above the ground it crosses.

Biblical Definition

The causeway was the raised ascent to the temple, and it appears in the assignment of the porters' wards under David: “To Shuppim and Hosah the lot came forth westward, with the gate Shallecheth, by the causeway of the going up, ward against ward” (1Ch 26:16), and “At Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar” (1Ch 26:18). The chapter is a duty roster. The porters were Levites, and their office was to keep the gates of the house of the LORD: “Among these were the divisions of the porters, even among the chief men, having wards one against another, to minister in the house of the LORD” (1Ch 26:12). Four gates, wards set opposite each other, lots cast for the stations, men posted on the raised road by which worshippers came up. The word mesillah is the same used by the prophet for a very different highway: “And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein” (Isa 35:8). Israel's roads went up to the house of God, and its prophets used the road as the picture of the way to Him.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a causey or causeway as a way raised above the natural level of the ground, by stones, earth or other materials, serving as a dry passage.

expand to see more

CAUSEWAY, CAU'SEY, n. A way raised above the natural level of the ground, by stones, earth, timber, fascines, etc., serving as a dry passage over wet or marshy ground.

2. A paved way; a raised road.

POR'TER, n. A man that has the charge of a door or gate; a doorkeeper.

WARD, n. Guard; watch; a garrison; the act of guarding; a station or post of guard.

Key Scripture

1 Chronicles 26:16 — "To Shuppim and Hosah the lot came forth westward, with the gate Shallecheth, by the causeway of the going up, ward against ward."

1 Chronicles 26:18 — "At Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar."

1 Chronicles 26:12 — "Among these were the divisions of the porters, even among the chief men, having wards one against another, to minister in the house of the LORD."

Isaiah 35:8 — "And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein."

Modern Corruption

The guarding of the door is despised as gatekeeping, and a house with no porters is called welcoming.

expand to see more

Chronicles takes a whole chapter to record who stood where at the gates of the house of God, and calls that standing a ministry: to minister in the house of the LORD. The office existed because a holy house has a threshold, and someone must know what may come in. The modern instinct treats every such office as exclusion for its own sake, and a church that has abolished its porters will find that it has not become more open but merely undefended. Guarding a door is not the opposite of welcoming people through it; the porters' whole business was to stand on the road by which worshippers came up.

Isaiah 35:8 shows what the raised road finally pictures, and it holds both truths at once. The way of holiness is closed — the unclean shall not pass over it — and it is astonishingly open: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein. A road so plain that a simple traveller cannot lose it, and so holy that the unclean cannot walk it. Only one thing reconciles those clauses, and it is the cleansing of the unclean, which is why the way is called by Him who said, I am the way, and no man cometh unto the Father but by me.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mesillah (H4546), a raised highway — 1 Chronicles 26:16, 18; Isaiah 35:8, 40:3; shoer (H7778), a porter or gatekeeper.

expand to see more

Hebrew mesillah (H4546) — a built-up highway; 1 Chronicles 26:16, Isaiah 35:8, Isaiah 40:3, Psalm 84:5 of the ways in the heart.

Hebrew shoer (H7778) — a gatekeeper, porter; the Levitical office of 1 Chronicles 26.

Hebrew mishmereth (H4931) — a watch, ward, charge; the wards set one against another.

Shallecheth, the gate named in 1 Chronicles 26:16, stood at the head of the causeway of the going up.

Isaiah uses the same word for the way of holiness, which the unclean may not walk and the simple cannot lose.

Usage

"“By the causeway of the going up, ward against ward”."

"“To minister in the house of the LORD” — said of doorkeepers."

"“The wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein”."
